title: Coding framework of metacognition intervention components and instructional methods

description: A novel observational coding scheme designed by the authors, based on the PAT theory and inspirations from Chiu (2008), applied utterance-by-utterance to videotaped and transcribed AUT sessions.

title: Coherence analysis framework and its six activity-trace measures

title: Cohort-relative z-score feature engineering

description: This analytic method combines temporal socio-semantic network analysis (tSSNA) and ordered network analysis (ONA) to analyze collaborative knowledge creation.
title: Combined tSSNA and ONA method

title: Common multilevel developmental framework for cross-study coordination

title: Comparative framework for longitudinal models differing in change processes, temporal structure, and measurement design

title: Comparative framework for model-tracing and constraint-based intelligent tutoring paradigms

title: CoMPAS framework: six forms modeling individual participation in collaborative learning

title: Component-based instructional design framework for analyzing ICT-supported writing interventions

title: Composable LLM workflow for educational survey analysis

description: The CP model, developed by Thum and Hauser (2015), is a flexible functional form for describing growth trends with marked seasonal patterns.
title: Compound Polynomial growth model

description: The review offers \"a comprehensive checklist of reporting criteria for intensive longitudinal methods\", integrating the APA Journal Article Reporting Standards, the Trull and Ebner-Priemer (2020) guidelines, and the review's own findings.
title: Comprehensive checklist of reporting criteria for intensive longitudinal studies

description: The authors recommend striving for a unified language, such as a formalisation strategy, in which different CSCL theories can be expressed, proposing the Bayesian framework as a formal language within reach for CSCL researchers.
title: Computational formalisation of CSCL theories using Bayesian models

description: Computational grounded theory integrates qualitative research with computational techniques to analyze large datasets systematically for theory development, addressing grounded theory's subjective interpretation and replication difficulties.
title: Computational grounded theory

title: Computational making framework (Rode et al., 2015)

description: The CoMSA conceptualizes educational differences through three logistic curve parameters.
title: CoMSA three-parameter logistic learning-curve model

title: Concept network analysis (knowledge structure analysis)

description: The article is grounded in a framework (from Reeves et al., 2016) in which \"The framework articulates three key PD program outcomes variables: GTA cognition; GTA teaching practice; and undergraduate student outcomes.\" These outcomes are posited to be linearly and probabilistically related: PD change
title: Conceptual framework for GTA professional development research and evaluation

description: The framework adapts a pretrained ViT with LoRA and derives a response-level confidence score from the stability of predictions under semantic-preserving test-time perturbations (crops, rotations).
title: Confidence-aware selective automated scoring framework

description: The article introduces 'confidence judgement', a novel measure defined as \"the accuracy of one's own judgement in relation to one's ability at an online or written test\", conceptualised as an aspect of metacognition.
title: Confidence judgement

description: A practical methodology for refining analytics tools with time-poor domain experts: the lecturer annotates AWA output pasted into Word using signal detection theory codes (True/False Positives/Negatives) in a 2×2 confusion matrix, with margin comments; the linguist responds in the shared document.
title: Confusion-matrix annotation by a domain expert as a rapid parser-refinement methodology

description: Consensus calibration treats recalibration as a divide-and-conquer Bayesian computation: each time period is calibrated independently and the period posteriors are combined without revisiting earlier data.
title: Consensus calibration

description: The paper formalizes consistency as the similarity between the targeted degree p_u(m) each platform sets for each principle m and the degree q(m) achieved in a learner's recommended list, measured as the complement of a weighted Manhattan distance.
title: Consistency–equality fairness metric for educational recommenders

description: The article uses \"Constraint-Based Modelling (CBM) to model the domain knowledge and generate student models\".
title: Constraint-Based Modelling (CBM)

description: A framework for evaluating the characteristics of psychological constructs prior to automated coding, grounded in educational psychology measurement practices and validity theories (Cronbach & Meehl, 1955; Kane, 2013; Messick, 1995).
title: Construct evaluation framework

description: The article develops and applies the construct-level predictive validity framework following Hunter, Schmidt and Le (2006): the estimate of the \"true predictor-outcome correlation\" between the underlying construct measured by a selection test and the underlying knowledge measured in later examinatio
title: Construct-level predictive validity (CLPV) framework for interpreting selection-measure validity

description: The article organises learner-generated questions through a constructivist framework drawing on Piaget and Vygotsky's theories, in which student inquiries are categorised into three roles: \"knowledge transmitter, facilitator and co-learner\".
title: Constructivist three-role taxonomy of learner-generated questions

description: Because effect sizes vary with the interval between measurement waves and there is no optimal interval, the article proposes testing lag0 paths within each wave as a practical check on design.
title: Contemporaneous (lag0) sensitivity analysis for selecting panel-design time intervals

description: The article presents a framework, developed in the author's 2000 review, holding that professionalism evaluation must attend to three elements: the \"context\" in which a behaviour occurs, \"conflict between equally worthy values\" such as honesty versus confidentiality, and the individual's \"resolution
title: Context, conflict, and resolution framework for evaluating professionalism

description: The article's scoring framework matches a student's response to an examiner-supplied model answer using semantic contextual search similarity, returning a similarity index of 0–1 that is multiplied by the item's allotted marks.
title: Contextual similarity scoring model for automated essay grading

description: The contingent shift framework, based on Wood et al.
title: Contingent shift framework for measuring scaffolding contingency in classroom interaction

description: The CCM is an extension of the NIDA cognitive diagnostic model that \"utilizes continuous variables instead of binary latent variables to represent attributes, thus it offers a more generalized diagnosis\" (Hong et al., 2015).
title: Continuous Conjunctive Model

description: The article organizes frameworks for conceptualizing instructional quality along a continuum adapted from Charalambous and Praetorius (2018), in which \"Senden et al.
title: Continuum for classifying instructional quality frameworks: generic, subject-specific, and hybrid

description: The review establishes a continuum of evaluative complexity (Table 4) ranking assessment approaches from knowledge-centred measurement to assessment at educational-systems level.
title: Continuum of evaluative complexity spanning ten levels from cognitive assessment to normative/consensus assessment

description: Building on Said (1993), the article defines contrapuntal reading as drawing out \"the logics of and resistances to empire and imperialism that are silent or marginally present\" in designs and theories.
title: Contrapuntal reading

description: The article argues that earlier transfer studies were unconvincing because training was too short and controls were missing.
title: Controlled asymptotic practice-curve method for transfer experiments

description: The review adopts Cook, Bordage and Schmidt's threefold classification of research purposes: \"description (what was carried out), justification (does it work), and finally, clarification (how does it work)\".
title: Cook, Bordage and Schmidt's description–justification–clarification typology

description: The Chronologically Ordered Dialogue & Features Used (CORDFU) chart is the development of the original annotated user log from the Ecolab evaluation for group use of multimedia.

description: CORDTRA stands for Chronologically-ordered Representations of Discourse and Tool-Related Activity.
title: CORDTRA diagrams for visually representing the chronology of tool use and discourse in collaborative learning analysis

description: The article introduces an angular-statistics framework in which item and test difficulty and discriminating values are obtained from the cosine of the angle between the observed score vector and the maximum possible score vector, involving inner products and vector lengths.
title: Cosine similarity framework

description: The article demonstrates applying health economics methods—net benefit regression and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves—to educational interventions.
title: Cost-effectiveness analysis with net benefit regression and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves

description: The paper's organizing framework splits system-prompt instructions into two kinds.
title: Countable versus dispositional prompt-rule audit

description: CourseGraph is a four-step methodology for automatically assessing whether an external course overlaps with courses in a home curriculum.
title: CourseGraph course-overlap detection methodology
